volumes.label: Earliest observations 1563–1582
volumes.notes: Codex A (Opera Omnia X); Leipzig, Rostock, Copenhagen, Hven; the 1563 Jupiter–Saturn conjunction note. Digitised: KB Digital Collections object77724.

volumes.label: Collectio observationum (Bartholin)
volumes.notes: Post-Tycho compilation by Erasmus Bartholin; not in the Dreyer Codex series; not digitised (reading-room only). Title: 'Collectio observationum Tychonis Brahei ab Anno 1563 … per Erasm. Bartholinum'. Observations omitted from the Historia Coelestis, including the comet observations. A secure Bartholin autograph.

volumes.label: Observations 1577–1582 (portrait & arms binding)
volumes.notes: Codex B (Opera Omnia X); Hven 1577–1582. Tycho's portrait and arms on the binding.

volumes.label: Seven comets 1577–1596 (mostly Tycho's hand; leaf 56 also Wittich's)
volumes.notes: Hven; seven comets 1577–1596, mostly in Tycho's hand. Leaf 56 is a directly comparable Tycho-vs-Wittich pair: Tycho's autograph 1577 comet observation alongside Paul Wittich's Oct 1580 comet observations A–E, the latter authenticated by Jakob Monau's signed attestation of 23 Oct 1600 (Rosen 1981 reproduces both hands, Ryc.1–2). This leaf is documented specimen by specimen in the Graphonomicon of Tycho Brahe, under the Paul Wittich discriminator.

volumes.notes: A hand other than the autograph comet volume (GKS 1826); possibly Longomontanus's (Dreyer), unconfirmed.

volumes.label: Observations 1582–1586
volumes.notes: Codex C (Opera Omnia X); Hven 1582–1586. Partly autograph; the autograph source recopied into the Vienna fair-copies of 1582–1586 (Cod. 10657–10661). ~10 inserted 4° leaves of Elias Olai's German observations at the end of 1584.

volumes.label: Theory of Sun; lunar/planetary obs 1585–1593
volumes.notes: Hven; theory and observations 1585–1593, in a hand other than Longomontanus's.

volumes.label: Observations 1587–1589 + fixed stars 1590–1594
volumes.notes: Codex D (Opera Omnia X); Hven. Sun/Moon/planets for 1587–1589 (1587–88 fixed stars absent; 1589 planetary runs only to 2 June) PLUS the fixed-star observations for 1590–1594 (the matching planetary records for those years are in Codex E / GKS 313). The V scribe copied these fixed stars in Codex D's order — the source of the 1589–91 fixed-star muddle in the Historia Coelestis.

volumes.label: Brass-quadrant observations 1589
volumes.notes: Hven; brass-quadrant observations 1589, by Elias Olai (Morsing).

volumes.label: Transcripts of 1593, 1590 and 1598–1600

scribe_attribution.basis: Transcripts spanning 1590–1600 — the period of Longomontanus's service, so he is the leading candidate for the engrossing hand, but this is a date-availability inference, not a confirmed identification.

volumes.notes: Codex K (Opera Omnia X). Three fascicles: Fasc. I = the 1593 observations (the ONLY substantial transcript of 1593 — the year whose Vienna fair-copy volume was lost, and which the Historia Coelestis therefore almost wholly omits); Fasc. II = 1590; Fasc. III = 1598, 1599, Jan 1600. The single most important KB volume for recovering what the fair-copying dropped.

volumes.label: Observations 1590–1594 (Sun, Moon, planets)
volumes.notes: Codex E (Opera Omnia X); Hven. Sun/Moon/planet observations for 1590–1594 (the fixed stars for these years are in Codex D / GKS 312). Four leaves of the 1593 observations are appended at its end (the rest of 1593 is in Codex K / GKS 1828).

volumes.label: Comets of 1590 & 1596
volumes.notes: Codex O (Opera Omnia X); Hven; comets of 1590 and 1596. The cometary originals from which the fair-copies of those observations were taken.

volumes.label: Planetary observations 1595
volumes.notes: Codex F (Opera Omnia X); Hven 1595. Complete; no observation missing.

volumes.label: Observations 1596–97 (Wandsbek); Kepler's declaration
volumes.notes: Codex G (Opera Omnia X); Hven and Wandsbek. 1597 begins on fol. 93; Tycho appended David Fabricius's autograph observations. Kepler's declaration to Tycho's heirs pasted inside the front cover. Digitised: KB Digital Collections object856355.

volumes.label: Wittenberg & Benátky observations 1598–1600
volumes.notes: Codex H (Opera Omnia X); Wandsbek, Wittenberg, Benátky. Two fascicles: the 2nd holds 1598 (ending with the 6 Aug 1598 Wandsbek lunar eclipse); the 1st holds 1599 (Wittenberg, then Prague) running on to 2 Feb 1600.

volumes.label: Fasciculus of Sun & planet observations + 1599–1600 calculations

scribe_attribution.basis: Same hand as GKS 1827; possibly Longomontanus, unconfirmed. (The volume's identity is itself disputed.)

volumes.dreyer_codex_note: Dreyer (Opera Omnia X) letters A. Coll. Reg. 1829 as his Codex L — the 214-leaf transcript of the 1585 observations — but the live KB catalogue describes GKS 1829 as a 1599–1600 fasciculus. The identification is probable, not asserted, pending a leaf-count or image check.
volumes.notes: Dreyer's Codex L — the 214-leaf transcript of the 1585 observations, copied from the Vienna fair-copy — is probably this volume under an imprecise modern title, but the identification is not asserted pending a leaf-count or image check, and the volume's identity remains an open question in the register. The live KB catalogue title (soeg.kb.dk; Ilsøe, Støbeskeen 1999, p.582) reads 'Tychonis Brahei Fasciculus Observationum Solis et Planetarum, subjuncto calculo Planetarum ex observationibus annorum 1599 et 1600', in the same hand (possibly Longomontanus) as GKS 1827, whereas Dreyer, Opera Omnia X, identifies A. Coll. Reg. 1829 as his 'Codex L'. The two descriptions are irreconcilable as one volume; neighbours GKS 1827/1828/1830 align Dreyer↔KB with no offset, so a post-Dreyer rebinding/renumbering is the likely cause. The volume is recorded here per the live KB catalogue. An exhaustive KB sweep (2026-05-31) finds no other candidate, and the catalogue title dates only the appended calculation, not the main observations.

volumes.label: Observations 1600–1601 (Benátky & Prague)
volumes.notes: Codex I (Opera Omnia X); Benátky and Prague. Ends fol. 151v with 11 Oct 1601; Kepler's hand records Tycho's final illness and death. Lacks the solar observation of 9 May 1601 and the computed Mercury position of 29 Apr 1601. Includes observations Kepler sent Tycho in 1600.

scribe_attribution.basis: An exile volume: Hven abandoned 1597 (Wandsbek, then Wittenberg). Longomontanus gone; no documented engrossing scribe. Unattributed — Eriksen and Tengnagel are weak, unconfirmed candidates.

volumes.notes: The neat yearly fair-copy of the 1598 observations (154 ll.), recopied from the nightly autograph protocols now at KB. Year fixed by ÖNB Tabulae codicum VI p.218 (leaf-count series) + Dreyer Opera Omnia X. KB original: Codex H, 2nd fascicle. One of the 19 Vienna apographa (vol. 16 of 19). Scribal attribution (documentary prior, grade D, NOT paleographically confirmed): An exile volume: Hven abandoned 1597 (Wandsbek, then Wittenberg). Longomontanus gone; no documented engrossing scribe. Unattributed — Eriksen and Tengnagel are weak, unconfirmed candidates.

scribe_attribution.basis: Longomontanus rejoined Tycho at Prague in 1600 and is again a candidate; Eriksen returning, Tengnagel present. A genuine multi-way split.

scribe_attribution.basis: Longomontanus with Tycho until his death (24 Oct 1601); Johannes Eriksen was Tycho's personal secretary by spring 1601 (Christianson). Both strong candidates; Tengnagel also present.
